body.statement: For arbitrary finite \(T,K,q\), can the projection of \(\{\mathbb E_D[\Phi_T\Phi_T^{\top}]:D\in\mathfrak D_T\}\) relevant to \(\mathbb E_D[u_Tu_T^{\top}]\) be characterized by a lag-sized necessary-and-sufficient family of parity and positivity inequalities with explicit sign-orbit recovery, and can that characterization yield a quantitative finite-horizon bound \(|V_{T,K}-R_e^2N_q^2|\le c(K,q,R_g,R_e)/T\)?
body.justification: This exposes the genuinely unresolved general-order content instead of presenting a generic orbit SDP as a closed-form solution.
body.gap: Bandeira and Kunisky characterize degree-four pseudomoments rather than genuine binary-law moments, and Manchester's input-design lift has an approximation gap.
body.consumer: A lag-sized certificate would permit exact finite-sample design optimization for multi-lag N-of-1 targets without enumerating \(2^T\) paths.

obligation.what_is_open: A lag-sized necessary-and-sufficient description of the genuine binary fourth-moment projection, with constructive sign-orbit recovery and a uniform finite-horizon rate certificate.
obligation.obstruction: Positivity of the lifted covariance and the parity inequalities used at one lag do not characterize the correlation polytope at general lag order. The exact orbit formulation remains exponential, and the stationary block argument by itself supplies a limit but not the requested uniform finite-horizon rate.
obligation.attempted: Reduced the feasible set to global-sign orbit weights, projected it through the exact quadratic-error map, checked the scalar parity collapse at one lag, and tested whether the Golay block covariance eliminates the finite-window boundary coordinates. The latter proves the stationary limit but does not furnish sign-orbit recovery for every feasible projected tensor.
obligation.partial_result:
A computable exact characterization is available at exponential, rather than lag-sized, scale.  Let \(\mathcal O_T\) be the set of global-sign orbits in \(\{-1,+1\}^T\), choose a representative \(x_o\) of each orbit, and let \(p_o\) be its total probability.  Then the relevant projected fourth-moment set is exactly
\[
\left\{
\sum_{o\in\mathcal O_T}p_o,u_T(x_o)u_T(x_o)^{\top}:
p_o\geq0,\quad \sum_op_o=1,\quad
\sum_op_o x_{o,s}x_{o,t}=0\ \text{for all }s<t
\right\}.
\]
Consequently \(V_{T,K}\) is computed exactly by minimizing
\[
\max\!\left\{TR_g^2\lambda_{\max}\!\left(\sum_op_o u_T(x_o)u_T(x_o)^{\top}\right),
T^2R_e^2\|F_{T,q}\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\right\}
\]
over the displayed simplex and linear moment constraints; an epigraph variable turns this into a finite semidefinite program.  The lag-one parity proof collapses this program to one scalar moment, and the stationary Golay construction proves convergence of its value for fixed \(K,q\).  What is not proved is a necessary-and-sufficient description having size controlled only by the lag order, sign-orbit recovery from such a description, or the requested uniform finite-horizon \(T^{-1}\) error bound.
